newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Macquarie sees limited franking effect.
newsitem.headline: Macquarie sees limited franking effect.

text.p: Investment bank and broking house Macquarie Bank Ltd expected changes to franking credits rules announced in the May Federal budget would have a minimal impact on the bank's future profits, the bank said on Monday.
But it said the changes may effect the bank's ability to fully frank the same level of dividends from 1999.

Earlier Macquarie reported a net profit for the year to March 31 of A$116.94 million, up from a A$93.2 million net profit in 1995/96 and above market expectations of about A$105 million. The bank set a 25 cent final dividend.
"This is a record result, reflecting solid contributions from all five business groups," Macquarie Bank Chairman David Clarke said in a statement accompanying the results.
"It reflects favourable market conditions and a good level of activity right across the Bank rather than large, one-off deals," he said.
Macquarie's full year dividend was 43 cents per share, representing a dividend payout ratio of 57 percent, and up from 36 cents per share the previous year.
Macquarie Managing Director Allan Moss said he was confident the bank would maintain or grow its market share.
Macquarie said its Equities Group more than doubled its contribution to the bank during a year of record market turnover.
Macquarie Equities internationl business grew rapidly and contribute significantly to the result. Macquarie Underwriting more than doubled the number of transactions for the year.

Remunerations expenses rose 22 percent in 1996/97, "reflecting a 14 percent increase in staff numbers and an increase in performance related payments in line with the excellent return on equity for the year."
The annual profit of A$116.94 million represented a return on average shareholders funds of 25.2 percent.
Moss said there were generally high levels of activity throughout the bank.

"Competition is tough, but we are maintaining a leading psosition in mergers and acquisitions, foreign exchange, bullion, base metals, futures, equities, property investment banking, infrastructure and structured finance," he said.
Moss said Macquarie expected its funds management and PUMA mortgage bonds business to enjoy good growth in the year ahead.
The biggest contributor to profit was Corporate Finance, with 28 percent of group profits, down from 33 percent in 1995/96.
Treasury and Commodities' profits were basically steady at 24 percent of group profits, while profits from Equities rose to 17 percent from nine percent.
Macquarie's shares were down one cent at A$9.45 at 10.50 a.m. (0050 GMT).
Macquarie said its shareholder base had broadened to about 3,400 from about 1,000 since its listing ten months ago.
